# Evaluating ensemble ocean forecasting systems

An ensemble forecast is a set of members sampling the uncertainty of a single forecast.
It is evaluated on two axes: how good the ensemble mean is, which is comparable to a deterministic forecast, and how well the spread of the members describes the actual forecast error.

All scores on this page cover the year 2024 over 52 weekly starts.
The observation scores use the version 2 observation basis of OceanBench, the same class 4 matchup as the deterministic scores.
The gridded scores use the quarter degree GLORYS reanalysis as reference.

Two ensembles are evaluated:

- **GloEns**: the Mercator Ocean physics ensemble, 50 members, started on Thursdays. Its gridded evaluation covers subsurface temperature and salinity only, with no surface fields.
- **GloNet2-ens-icp**: the GloNet2 machine learning ensemble, 8 members with perturbed initial conditions, started on Wednesdays. It runs to lead day 9.

The deterministic GLONET2 forecast is shown next to the ensemble means as a baseline.

```{python}
#| output: false

import json
from helpers.ensemble_scores import ensemble_scores

ensemble_scores_json = json.dumps(ensemble_scores())
```

```{python}
#| output: asis

print(f'<script type="application/json" id="ensemble-scores-data">{ensemble_scores_json}</script>')
```

::: {#ensemble-scores}

## Classical view: ensemble means and the deterministic baseline

### Against observations

Root mean square error against the version 2 observation basis, global.
The ensemble rows are the error of the ensemble mean, the GLONET2 rows are the error of the single deterministic member.
The deterministic class 4 aggregate keeps its own depth bins, which do not match the ensemble depth bands, so the rows of a variable are not paired one to one.
GloEns has no current observations in its ensemble evaluation.
Temperature errors are differences, so kelvin and degrees Celsius carry the same number.

<div id="ensemble-observations-rmsd"></div>

### Against GLORYS

Root mean square difference of the ensemble mean against the 2024 [GLORYS reanalysis](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_PHY_001_030), global, on the native model depth levels.
GloEns carries no surface fields here, so sea surface height and surface temperature appear for GloNet2-ens-icp only.
GloNet2-ens-icp stops at lead day 9, so its lead day 10 cells are empty.

<div id="ensemble-gridded-rmsd"></div>

## Probabilistic metrics

The fair continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) rewards a sharp and reliable ensemble and is expressed in the unit of the variable, lower is better.
The spread error ratio compares the ensemble spread with the error of the ensemble mean: one is a reliable ensemble, below one means the ensemble is under dispersive.

### Against observations

The observation space spread error ratio is additive: the observation error variance is added to the ensemble variance before the ratio is taken.

<div id="ensemble-observations-crps"></div>

<div id="ensemble-observations-ssr"></div>
